core.why: the core sources are committed; comments and inline #[cfg(test)] modules are out of scope, because a comment naming a banned string and a test asserting the ban must not trip the rule they document

app-src.why: the renderer and shell sources are committed; comments and *.test.* files are out of scope for the same reason

rules.why: Phase 1 has no destructive operation at all. The token FORGET appears in no rendered string, no accessible name and no command name; a build that ships it has shipped the control. The source-side complement is scripts/check-destructive-tokens.mjs, which cannot reach the built bundle because it refuses a gitignored scan root by design.

Quick switch's footer prints the two keycap glyphs the target keyboards actually carry. The Option and Space glyphs are not among them, and a keycap a keyboard does not print is an instruction the user cannot follow.
The superseded Locations footer asserts the inference §1.1 forbids: a fork and its upstream share a root commit by definition, so a shared root commit cannot say one project rather than n.
Phase 1 compares copies by identity, never by direction. A directional claim needs a merge-base across two object stores, which needs a fetch, which §17 forbids — so the product may not render one.
Never reward volume. J4 produces commit-days; nothing in the schema stores a count, and the superseded legend naming commits by the user is the string that would make one worth acquiring.
The first-run escape control is short, in the first rendered frame and reachable by Tab. The superseded sentence is longer than the control it labels and was replaced for that reason.
Nothing renders when no roast clause matches — silence, not a reassurance. The superseded strings either fill that silence or carry an age §5.6's clause table no longer produces.
patterns: when it was last looked at

rules.why: The design's band vocabulary is forbidden in every machine-readable surface: a CSS class, a query field, a protocol message, a log line or an accessible name. The two enum words that look like band names are NOT banned — §11.7 requires them verbatim in an accessible name, so a grep for those would fail a correct build.

The bounded worktree watch set does watch inside a repository — it invalidates the worktree observation time. The sentence claiming otherwise is false against §6 and would be a currency claim the product cannot make.
patterns: Nothing is watched inside a repository

rules.why: Probe C moved the canvas layer, the texture atlas and layer swim to phase 3, and criterion 22 dropped its GPU clause on that basis. Nothing asserted DOM-only rendering, which is how a negative rule comes back by accident.

Plan 12 owns the token vocabulary and the stylesheet gate; the ladder is closed there, with §7.3a's language palette and everything the rasterizer computes exempt by name. A second implementation here would drift from the vocabulary file it reads.

The motion half is the same grep over the same built stylesheet against §11.6's two tables plus the named single-effect values, and plan 12's script already carries both allowlists. A beat is a band, so the allowlist is data the owning script holds, not a pattern this file can restate.

An inset box-shadow ring is the only focus indicator that survives clip-path clipping every outline away, so a rule removing the outline without a replacement in the same rule kills the keyboard silently. Plan 12 owns the CSS-rule parser this needs.
The retired half-pixel size is one member of the scale-membership check plan 12 already runs over every computed font-size, and the floor is only meaningful alongside the scale and its tracking.
The default palette chord is the Windows system window menu accelerator, which is why plan 15 gates it over the built shell bundle. One chord, one grep, one owner.

No scope string is written in renderer source. The list the CONNECTED state draws comes from accounts.list's grantedScopes, which is read back from the server, because a hard-coded list is how two scope names that do not exist came to be drawn on a settings screen. The patterns are substrings, so `workflow` subsumes `workflow:read`. Its limitation is part of the rule: the bare string `repo` is NOT bannable, being an unavoidable English word, and that is precisely why the displayed list must come from the payload and not from a grep's silence.

pendingRegistryEntry.why: This plan's Task 15 registers AC-P2-20-3 and removes this escape; the rule lands with the deletion it is the gate for, several tasks earlier.
